title: Indices Near a Key Value
statement:
You get an integer array nums, a value key and a reach k. An index i is near the key when some index j with nums[j] === key satisfies |i − j| ≤ k. An index that holds the key is near it (take j = i).

Return every index that is near the key, in increasing order, each listed once. The key appears in nums at least once.

examples.why: The key sits at index 2 only, and reach 1 covers indices 1 to 3.
Index 1 covers 0 to 3 and index 4 covers 2 to 5. Indices 2 and 3 are covered twice but listed once.
With reach 0 an index is near only if it holds the key itself.

hints: Each key position covers a block of indices. What does the union of those blocks look like?
Blocks from key positions further right start further right. If you remember the last index you already emitted, where should the next block start?
For each key position j, emit indices from max(lastEmitted + 1, j − k) to min(n − 1, j + k). Each index is emitted at most once.

explain.intuition:
Every key position j covers the block [j − k, j + k], clipped to the array. The answer is the union of these blocks. Blocks overlap, and naively adding all of them can cost O(n · k) and produce duplicates.

Because key positions are visited left to right, their blocks also start left to right. Keep one pointer, the next index not yet emitted. For each block, start from whichever is later, that pointer or the block's start, and run to the block's end. The pointer only moves forward, so every index is touched at most once: two pointers, one over key positions and one over output indices.
steps: Set next = 0, the smallest index not yet emitted, and an empty result.
Scan j from 0 to n − 1. Skip it unless nums[j] === key.
Emit every index from max(next, j − k) to min(n − 1, j + k).
Set next to one past the last emitted index. Return the result.
pitfalls: Emitting each block in full and then deduplicating. It is O(n · k) and the output is no longer sorted without extra work.
Forgetting to clip at 0 and n − 1, which emits negative indices or indices past the end.
Reading the condition as |i − j| < k. The reach includes distance exactly k.

solutions.title: Check a window around every index
solutions.idea: For each index, look at the 2k + 1 indices around it and stop at the first key.

solutions.title: Merge the blocks with a moving pointer
solutions.idea: Visit key positions in order and emit only the part of each block that has not been emitted yet.

followups: Answer many queries (key, k) on the same array. What would you precompute?
Return the indices as merged ranges [start, end] instead of one by one.
